title: Moving on Up: 42.22 Pre-Release
raw:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4460946/93e15217f7f408fe238c0948b7182b5263b66144.png"][/img]
Hello again, Survivors!

We have news on the upcoming 42.22 Update, available for testing now on our new Pre-Release branch, which replaces the Unstable branch for early testing. Yes, we changed the branch name, as it was causing some confusion among players, especially given the (long) history of Unstable in Build 42.

What does this mean to you? For the average player, absolutely nothing. We recommend you keep on enjoying Project Zomboid on the default Stable branch, currently 42.21, while pre-release goes through final vetting.

If, however, you are a [b]modder, a multiplayer server admin[/b] or just the [b]brave, testing-friendly[/b] type who is willing to test and break things before they go live to the broader public, then you can opt-in to the Pre-Release.

[/p][h2]How to update Project Zomboid to access Pre-Release[/h2][p]
1. Back up any Project Zomboid save games you want to come back to, just in case.
2. Right-click Project Zomboid in your Steam Library.
3. Select “Properties”.
4. Under “Game Versions & Betas” select “Pre-Release”

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4460946/42fe75af2aa84c414d48e4f4b7971a7056f0b16c.gif"][/img]
Going forward, we’ll be releasing builds into the Pre-Release branch before they go forward to the Stable branch (barring urgent hotfixes that may need to go directly to Stable). The goal here is to identify any issues that need to be addressed, while also allowing server admins and modders a chance to look under the hood for upcoming changes. We plan on [b]keeping a build in the Pre-Release branch for at least one week[/b] before it moves to the Stable branch.

We really want to stress though; [b]don’t move your long-term singleplayer save over to the Pre-Release branch[/b] [i][b]unless you have backed up that save[/b][/i]! We cannot guarantee that the save will work and/or you will be able to use it in the final release, which will come after Pre-Release testing is complete.

In summary, the cycle for a new update is:

[i]New update released -> deployed to [b]Pre-Release[/b] branch -> Tested, one week minimum -> deployed to [b]Stable[/b] branch.[/i]

If, during Pre-Release testing, bugs are discovered that would benefit from another revision of the update, we’ll do that, and keep you in the loop if it happens via our community channels (our [url="https://theindiestone.com/forums/"]forums[/url], [url="https://www.reddit.com/r/projectzomboid/"]Reddit[/url] and [url="https://discord.gg/theindiestone"]Discord[/url] primarily).

But what’s actually [i]in[/i] this new update?
